title: Review Artifact
description: The durable, persisted record of a flow-review effort for ONE repo — one JSON+MD pair per repo, never merged across repos (cross-repo work produces N sibling files). Unlike review-finding-report.schema.json (one reviewer's single-round emission to the orchestrator), this file AGGREGATES every reviewer's findings across every round into one evolving document, created once at first review and updated in place thereafter. This file defines the SHAPE only; the SEMANTICS (the swarm dispatch, the fix-loop handoff to flow-implementation) live in flow-review and review-report-standards; the merge/verdict arithmetic for this persisted artifact is owned by flow-review/scripts/lib/review-aggregates.jq. The orchestrator is the sole writer — a reviewer never writes this file directly; it returns findings as review-finding-report.schema.json today, and the orchestrator merges them in here. One JSON object per file, at `.crucible/docs/reviews/{year}/{month}/{day}/{repo-or-effort-slug}.json`.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Pinned so a consumer can detect a shape change. The document is durable and may outlive a revision.

id.description: The repo-or-effort slug — matches the filename (without extension).

repo.description: Which repo/component this artifact covers. Always exactly one — cross-repo work produces N sibling files, never a merged one.

spec_ref.description: Path to the flow-spec artifact this effort's implementation was built against, if one governed it. OMITTED (never null) when no spec exists.

created.description: ISO 8601 date only — when this review effort STARTED (round 1). Never changed by later rounds; the folder path shares this convention.

last_updated.description: ISO 8601 date only — the most recent round's date. Updated in place each round.

diff_files.description: The diff this review covers, cumulative across rounds, sorted by path and unique by path: the repo-relative paths flow-review/scripts/diff-scope.sh wrote, as {path, sha} objects when the writer was given diff-files.tsv and plain path strings when given diff-files.txt (diff-file.schema.json). review-create.sh sets it from round 1's list; review-add-round.sh merges each round's list in by path, the newer entry winning (each round's own list is rounds[].diff_files). The writers check the locations they accept at write time against the round's own list: every location a new finding gives, every location an update adds to a stored finding, every speculative location and every new handoff location names one of the paths (minus a trailing :line or :start-end) or is anchored by its own entry's relates_to on a line the diff changed (diff-hunks.tsv); a finding carried from an earlier round is not re-checked against a later list, but review-add-round.sh sets one RESOLVED only when one of its files is in that round's list. OPTIONAL in this shape; an artifact without it gains it on its next round (review-add-round.sh).

plan_review.description: OPTIONAL. Present (true) when the artifact records the review of a flow-testing test plan (review-create.sh --plan-review): a location may then be plan:<item> (plan:test-3, plan:not_tested-1, plan:B2), in scope without naming a diff file and covered for a resolution. review-add-round.sh takes --plan-review exactly when it is set. Only the value true is written.

snapshot.description: OPTIONAL. The tree sha flow-review/scripts/diff-scope.sh --snapshot-out recorded, when the reviewed diff was taken since that snapshot (review-create.sh --snapshot). Not rendered.

rounds.description: One entry per review round that has run, in order. A light history log for traceability — not a full per-finding change log (git history of this file already provides that if the file is committed).

overall_verdict.description: Counting rule: review-report-standards, Verdict Arithmetic. Computed by flow-review/scripts/lib/review-aggregates.jq.

summary.description: Counting rule: review-report-standards, Verdict Arithmetic. Computed by flow-review/scripts/lib/review-aggregates.jq.

handoffs.description: OPTIONAL. Concerns one reviewer passed to another seat, in the order recorded, each open until ruled once (review-create.sh / review-add-round.sh). Omitted when there are none. Never counted toward the verdict.

reviewers.description: Which reviewer/lens agents were dispatched this round.

diff_files.description: OPTIONAL. The diff this round was given (review-add-round.sh's --diff-files), in the form of the top-level diff_files; absent on round 1, whose list is the top-level diff_files as created.

speculative.description: OPTIONAL. This round's speculative concerns (review-core, Realism test); not findings. Omitted when the round recorded none. Counting rule: review-report-standards, Verdict Arithmetic.

speculative_entry.$comment: review-finding-report.schema.json's speculative_entry plus `key`, `reviewer`, `recheck` and `promoted_to`, inlined for the same additionalProperties:false reason as `finding` below.

key.description: The entry's key: the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of `reviewer|location|concern`, computed by the writer (review-create.sh, review-add-round.sh; review-update-status.sh keys a stored entry without one), the same in every round that repeats the entry. The <key> of render-md.sh's REVIEW_ITEM_<n>=speculative:<key> and of review-update-status.sh --speculative-key. Never taken from a reviewer report. OPTIONAL in this shape: an entry stored without one is keyed by the next writer.

reviewer.description: Which reviewer/lens agent raised this concern.

location.description: One `file:line` (or `file:start-end`) site — the same locator form as a finding's locations.

concern.description: ONE line: the concern as the reviewer would have raised it.

why_speculative.description: ONE line: what the concern would need that is not in evidence.

category.description: The reviewer's category for the concern, from its own vocabulary (x-reviewers in contracts/review-category.schema.json; the union of every vocabulary for a reviewer it does not list): required on every entry a writer records, and in that vocabulary (writer-enforced); OPTIONAL in this shape, so a stored entry without one is read as it is. A category flagged security in contracts/review-category.schema.json (x-categories) puts the item under the security floor: proof alone, never unproven (writer-enforced); once there, the item is recorded security_floor: true and stays under the floor — a later change to a non-security category is refused (writer-enforced). An item whose text names a security weakness listed in x-security-terms (a finding's problem or trigger, a speculative entry's concern) is refused under a category that is not a security one (writer-enforced). A repeat of the entry in a later round whose category, proof or unproven changed starts fresh: it carries no re-check or promotion from the earlier copy; otherwise it carries a pending re-check, and the finding it was promoted to while that finding is open.

real_if.description: OPTIONAL. ONE line of at most 100 characters: the evidence that would make the concern real (review-core, Realism test). No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

relates_to.description: OPTIONAL. ONE `file:line` (or `file:start-end`) location of at most 300 characters whose line, or whole range, lies inside one hunk the diff changed (diff-scope.sh's diff-hunks.tsv): the changed code that relies on or exposes a defect located outside the diff. A location outside the diff is accepted only when its own entry's relates_to is on a changed line, and a relates_to given always is (writer-enforced at write time). No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

proof.description: OPTIONAL in this shape; writer-enforced: every speculative entry carries exactly one of proof or unproven, and under the security floor (reviewer lens-security-reviewer, or a security category) proof alone — a security concern stays realistic until proven harmless. ONE line of at most 100 characters: the evidence that the item is not real or harmless, named as a file:line locator whose file is path-like — it holds a letter and has an extension, a "/", or is Makefile, Dockerfile, Justfile, Rakefile, Gemfile or Procfile — and is no part of a URL (src/a.rs:42, src/a.rs:42-50, Makefile:3; never 10:30), naming a regular file under the writer's --repo-root and a line within it (writer-enforced), or in a test-plan review (plan_review) also a test number the reviewed plan holds (test 3; resolved against the writer's --plan). No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

unproven.description: OPTIONAL in this shape; writer-enforced as for proof, which it excludes: the item is set aside without proof. Only the value true is written.

recheck.description: OPTIONAL. The human's record of re-checking this set-aside item, set only through flow-review/scripts/review-update-status.sh --recheck; never taken from a reviewer report.

security_floor.description: OPTIONAL. Recorded by the flow-review writers, never taken from a reviewer report: the item has been under the security floor (reviewer lens-security-reviewer, or a security category). It stays there whatever later changes: proof alone, never unproven, and its category stays a security one (writer-enforced).

promoted_to.description: OPTIONAL. The id of the finding this entry was promoted to after its re-check survived or escalated it to the human, set only through flow-review/scripts/review-update-status.sh --promote-to-id; never taken from a reviewer report. A promoted entry is listed, counted and re-checked only as that finding.

finding.$comment: Duplicates review-finding-report.schema.json's finding shape (id/status/severity/category/locations/first_seen/problem/fix, with realism/trigger/realism_reason OPTIONAL here — an absent realism means realistic) rather than composing via allOf, plus adds reviewer/tracked_status/addressed_in_round/realism_confirmed/realism_confirmed_severity/recheck/resolution_proof/ack_reason: that base finding has additionalProperties:false, and allOf does not extend a closed schema cleanly (the base's additionalProperties:false evaluates against the whole instance, so a sibling allOf branch adding new properties fails validation). Same pattern — document-and-inline rather than compose — as external-review-advocate-verdict.schema.json vs finding-verdict.schema.json (there the reason is a narrower enum subset, not an additionalProperties/allOf conflict, but both cases choose to duplicate-and-explain over forcing a $ref).

id.description: Stable, reviewer-prefixed identifier; ID stability (assignment/reuse/renumbering) is owned by review-report-standards. Same convention as review-finding-report.schema.json.

reviewer.description: Which reviewer/lens agent raised this finding. Present here (unlike review-finding-report.schema.json, where it's a top-level field) because this document aggregates multiple reviewers. Fixed once written: an update never changes it (writer-enforced).

status.description: Cross-round finding identity (is it still current) — shared with review-finding-report.schema.json.

tracked_status.description: Where the fix currently sits in the human/tech-pair workflow. Orthogonal to `status` — see tracked-status.schema.json for why these are two fields, not one.

realism.description: OPTIONAL. review-core, Realism test; ABSENT means realistic. Counting rule: review-report-standards, Verdict Arithmetic.

realism_confirmed.description: OPTIONAL. The human's confirmation of an edge-case finding, set only through flow-review/scripts/review-update-status.sh --confirm-edge-case; never taken from a reviewer report. Present only alongside realism edge-case. Counting rule: review-report-standards, Verdict Arithmetic.

realism_confirmed_severity.description: OPTIONAL. The severity realism_confirmed was given at, set and cleared with it by the flow-review scripts; a different current severity voids the confirmation. Counting rule: review-report-standards, Verdict Arithmetic.

trigger.description: OPTIONAL. ONE line: the concrete real-use scenario that makes the problem happen (review-core, Realism test).

realism_reason.description: OPTIONAL. ONE line of at most 100 characters: why the finding is classed edge-case (review-core, Realism test). Allowed on any finding; rendered only beside an open edge case. No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

category.description: Sub-lens tag from the reviewer's own controlled vocabulary: one of its list in x-reviewers of contracts/review-category.schema.json, or of the union of every vocabulary for a reviewer it does not list (writer-enforced). A category flagged security in contracts/review-category.schema.json (x-categories) puts the item under the security floor: proof alone, never unproven (writer-enforced); once there, the item is recorded security_floor: true and stays under the floor — a later change to a non-security category is refused (writer-enforced). An item whose text names a security weakness listed in x-security-terms (a finding's problem or trigger, a speculative entry's concern) is refused under a category that is not a security one (writer-enforced).

locations.description: One or more `file:line` (or `file:start-end`) sites, each one line. An array because a finding may span sites (e.g. duplication). A site outside the diff needs its own entry's relates_to on a changed line. In a test-plan review (plan_review), a site may also be plan:<item>.

relates_to.description: OPTIONAL. ONE `file:line` (or `file:start-end`) location of at most 300 characters whose line, or whole range, lies inside one hunk the diff changed (diff-scope.sh's diff-hunks.tsv): the changed code that relies on or exposes a defect located outside the diff. A location outside the diff is accepted only when its own entry's relates_to is on a changed line, and a relates_to given always is (writer-enforced at write time). No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

proof.description: OPTIONAL in this shape; writer-enforced: an edge-case finding carries exactly one of proof or unproven — kept through every reclassification and confirmation — and under the security floor (reviewer lens-security-reviewer, or a security category) proof alone — a security concern stays realistic until proven harmless. ONE line of at most 100 characters: the evidence that the item is rare or harmless. A proof names its evidence as a file:line locator whose file is path-like — it holds a letter and has an extension, a "/", or is Makefile, Dockerfile, Justfile, Rakefile, Gemfile or Procfile — and is no part of a URL (src/a.rs:42, src/a.rs:42-50, Makefile:3; never 10:30), naming a regular file under the writer's --repo-root and a line within it (writer-enforced), or in a test-plan review (plan_review) also a test number the reviewed plan holds (test 3; resolved against the writer's --plan), or, recorded by the orchestrator only (review-update-status.sh --proof), as text starting "ran " (a command and its result); a reviewer fields-file never gives that form (writer-enforced). No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

unproven.description: OPTIONAL in this shape; writer-enforced as for proof, which it excludes: the item is set aside without proof. Only the value true is written.

recheck.description: OPTIONAL. The human's record of re-checking this set-aside item (an edge-case finding), set only through flow-review/scripts/review-update-status.sh --recheck; never taken from a reviewer report.

security_floor.description: OPTIONAL. Recorded by the flow-review writers, never taken from a reviewer report: the item has been under the security floor (reviewer lens-security-reviewer, or a security category). It stays there whatever later changes: proof alone, never unproven, and its category stays a security one (writer-enforced).

resolution_proof.description: OPTIONAL in this shape; writer-enforced: present when the finding was set RESOLVED by a writer that requires it (review-update-status.sh --resolution-proof, a review-add-round.sh entry setting RESOLVED), and dropped when the finding leaves RESOLVED. ONE line of at most 100 characters: the evidence the fix holds, named as a file:line locator whose file is path-like — it holds a letter and has an extension, a "/", or is Makefile, Dockerfile, Justfile, Rakefile, Gemfile or Procfile — and is no part of a URL (src/a.rs:42, src/a.rs:42-50, Makefile:3; never 10:30), naming a regular file under the writer's --repo-root and a line within it (writer-enforced), or in a test-plan review (plan_review) also a test number the reviewed plan holds (test 3; resolved against the writer's --plan), or, recorded by the orchestrator only (review-update-status.sh --resolution-proof), as text starting "ran " (a command and its result). No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

ack_reason.description: OPTIONAL in this shape; writer-enforced: present when the finding was set ACK through review-update-status.sh --status ACK --reason (the human's reason for waiving it, in their words), and dropped when the finding leaves ACK; never taken from a reviewer report. An ACK finding stored before the field existed carries none. ONE line of at most 200 characters. No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

first_seen.description: ISO 8601 date only, frozen at creation; kept unchanged across rounds.

problem.description: ONE line: what is wrong. Never restate large code.

fix.description: ONE line: the concrete remedy the implementer should apply.

addressed_in_round.description: Which round (per `rounds`) the tech pair's fix was verified. OMITTED (never null) while tracked_status is PENDING or IN_PROGRESS.

recheck.description: A re-check of a set-aside item — an edge-case finding, a speculative entry or a handoff (review-update-status.sh --recheck): pending; survived or cleared with the one-line proof of the outcome; escalated to the human with the one-line reason the re-check could not settle it (the verifier's or the adversary's unresolved disagreement), in plain words; or, on a speculative entry only, dismissed by the human with their reason, in their words. An outcome is recorded once per item (writer-enforced), except that an escalated speculative entry is closed by the human: promoted to a NEW finding through review-update-status.sh --promote-to-id (as a survived one is), or dismissed through --recheck dismissed --reason, which is refused on an entry under the security floor. Never counted toward the verdict; an escalated one not yet decided, and a survived one on a confirmed edge case, mark the item as needing the human's decision; a dismissed one, and an escalated one on a finding the human has since decided (decided), do not.

proof.description: Present exactly when status is survived or cleared (writer-enforced): ONE line of at most 100 characters, the evidence of the outcome from a reviewer or the review-arbiter, named as a file:line locator whose file is path-like — it holds a letter and has an extension, a "/", or is Makefile, Dockerfile, Justfile, Rakefile, Gemfile or Procfile — and is no part of a URL (src/a.rs:42, src/a.rs:42-50, Makefile:3; never 10:30), naming a regular file under the writer's --repo-root and a line within it (writer-enforced), or in a test-plan review (plan_review) also a test number the reviewed plan holds (test 3; resolved against the writer's --plan); never a "ran " form (writer-enforced). No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

reason.description: Present exactly when status is escalated or dismissed (writer-enforced): ONE line of at most 200 characters, in plain words — for escalated, why the re-check escalated the item to the human (the verifier's or the adversary's unresolved disagreement); for dismissed, the human's reason for dismissing it, in their words. No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

round.description: The newest recorded round when the re-check was recorded.

decided.description: OPTIONAL. On an escalated re-check of a finding only: the human decided the finding after the escalation was recorded — review-update-status.sh --confirm-edge-case, --realism realistic or --status ACK on it — so it no longer needs the human's decision; the finding still counts toward the verdict as its status, realism and severity say. Only the value true is written, by review-update-status.sh; a review-add-round.sh update that changes the finding's evidence drops the re-check with it.

handoff.description: A concern one reviewer passed to another seat (review-core). open until ruled once — by a round (review-add-round.sh, an entry whose index is the handoff's 1-based place in handoffs) or by the orchestrator (review-update-status.sh --handoff-index N --ruling, N the same 1-based place, the <N> of render-md.sh's REVIEW_ITEM_<n>=handoff:<N>) — as filed (as the finding filed_as names), rejected, or out-of-scope, each with its proof; or waived by the human, only through review-update-status.sh --handoff-index N --ruling waived --reason, with the human's reason in their words. A new location outside the diff needs its own relates_to on a changed line, as for a finding (writer-enforced).

from.description: The reviewer/lens agent that passed the concern on.

to.description: The reviewer/lens seat the concern was passed to.

concern.description: ONE line: the concern as passed on.

relates_to.description: OPTIONAL. As a finding's relates_to: its line, or whole range, inside one hunk the diff changed.

proof.description: Present exactly when ruling is filed, rejected or out-of-scope (writer-enforced): ONE line of at most 100 characters, the evidence behind the ruling from the seat or the review-arbiter, named as a file:line locator whose file is path-like — it holds a letter and has an extension, a "/", or is Makefile, Dockerfile, Justfile, Rakefile, Gemfile or Procfile — and is no part of a URL (src/a.rs:42, src/a.rs:42-50, Makefile:3; never 10:30), naming a regular file under the writer's --repo-root and a line within it (writer-enforced), or in a test-plan review (plan_review) also a test number the reviewed plan holds (test 3; resolved against the writer's --plan); never a "ran " form (writer-enforced).

filed_as.description: Present exactly when ruling is filed: the id of the finding the concern was filed as, which the artifact holds (writer-enforced).

reason.description: Present exactly when ruling is waived (writer-enforced): the human's reason for waiving the handoff, in their own words — free text, not a proof form. ONE line of at most 200 characters. No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

recheck.description: OPTIONAL. The human's record of re-checking this handoff, set only through flow-review/scripts/review-update-status.sh --handoff-index N --recheck; never taken from a reviewer report. An open handoff whose re-check was escalated needs the human's decision.

findings.problem: jobId path param not validated as UUID before the repository lookup
findings.fix: validate against a UUID regex before querying; return 400 on mismatch

findings.problem: parameter named `data` conveys nothing about its shape
findings.fix: rename to `jobInput`, matching the spec's `input` field
